transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-24
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 61 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Nora Singh (Procurement), Evan Morales (InfoSec), Priya Raman (Eng Manager), Samir Patel (FinOps), Olivia Chen (Legal)
----
Summary: A focused procurement/legal/tech alignment to resolve KMS/privileged keying questions, billing and egress estimates, and specific DPA variant requirements for AstraCove's pilot environment. The call includes clarifying required audit logs, encryption-at-rest key custody (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed), and pricing guardrails for the initial pilot.
Topics: KMS options, DPA clauses for PII, SLA expectations (uptime and latency targets), billing model for burst capacity and egress, SOC2 and audit artifacts, pilot scope and timeline.
Action items: see metadata list above.
----
Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run about an hour, quick intros and then dive into the KMS and billing items that Nora flagged.
[00:12] Nora Singh: Thanks Maya, appreciate it. We're trying to accelerate vendor onboarding but need clarity on who holds keys and how audit logs are exposed before procurement greenlights any charges.
[00:20] Daniel Cho: Hey all, Daniel from Redwood, I'll cover the technical KMS flow and what we can support in Private and Dedicated. Quick note, sometimes in transcripts our product name comes out wrong—if you see "Redwood Runtime" called something else, that's just the transcription.
[00:34] Evan Morales: Good. Our main constraints: HSM-backed keys in our cloud KMS (we use CloudGuard KMS) and we need read-only audit consumption for security ops; no vendor-managed plaintext keying.
[00:46] Priya Raman: From engineering, latency SLO matters — we can't spike beyond 200ms p95 for key-fetch ops in the hot path. If KMS calls add variability, we need a path to cache or use envelope encryption.
[01:00] Maya Patel: That's fair. Two supported modes: 1) Redwood-managed keys with customer-supplied wrapped keys (we can do BYOK-like flow), 2) Customer-managed keys where the customer KMS signs/unwraps on their side — in private deployments we can do full KMIP/HSM integration. There's also an envelope pattern to reduce on-path calls.
[01:18] Samir Patel: For finance, we need to understand any premium for privileged key management. Is there a separate charge for KMS integration or just normal dedicated pricing? Also egress — what's the expected billback model?
[01:30] Daniel Cho: We'll provide a pricing delta for the Dedicated+KMS path. Typically KMS integration isn't a hard additional recurring fee but it can add engineering onboarding hours; the bigger drivers are dedicated GPU pool sizing and egress. For egress we show two components: intra-region traffic (negligible) vs customer download/export (charged per GB).
[01:47] Olivia Chen: On DPA language: we probably need a variant that explicitly disallows Redwood from holding unencrypted customer data keys. Also, audit log retention periods must be 7 years for regulated lines — can Redwood commit to that or provide exportable logs?
[02:02] Maya Patel: We can commit to exporting audit logs to a customer S3 or to a syslog endpoint; retention on Redwood's side is configurable. Seven years is longer than our default retention so we'd need to discuss retention add-on or customer-managed archival. I'll flag this for legal.
[02:18] Nora Singh: Procurement will need a clear entry in the SOW for retention fees if that's the case — prefer transparent line items.
[02:25] Liam O'Connor: From CS, we usually run a 4-week pilot with masked data or a scoped PII set — that helps with both security review and billing predictability. We can instrument token-level cost estimates during that pilot.
[02:38] Priya Raman: Masking is fine for initial evals, but the final rollout will need unmasked telemetry for model quality checks. So the DPA needs to allow controlled unmasked flows under contractual obligations.
[02:51] Daniel Cho: Technically, for unmasked telem we recommend using our Private control-plane option where the control-plane sits in your VPC; logs and keys never leave your network. There's also a Dedicated option with per-customer GPU pool but keys can be proxied. Both patterns will satisfy different infosec constraints.
[03:10] Evan Morales: Can you describe the key lifecycle for the envelope encryption pattern? I want to see whether we still make calls to Redwood-managed endpoints.
[03:18] Daniel Cho: Sure — high level: customer KMS issues data key, Redwood runtime receives only encrypted data keys, the runtime caches decrypted data keys in memory for a configurable TTL (e.g., 1 hour) and uses them for token encryption. We never persist plaintext keys. If you require no plaintext on Redwood side, we can adopt a proxy pattern where decryption happens in a sidecar inside your VPC. That increases latency but meets custody requirements.
[03:37] Priya Raman: The in-memory cache TTL — can we set it to zero for strict compliance? That will increase KMS calls though.
[03:45] Daniel Cho: Yes you can. Zero TTL means every job will re-fetch, so add latency and cost. We'll document the trade-off.
[03:53] Samir Patel: Regarding costs, is there an estimate of how much KMS calls would add to the per-request cost? We need a ballpark to approve pilot spend.
[04:02] Daniel Cho: Rough ballpark: a KMS decrypt call is inexpensive in compute but if you call it per inference it grows linearly. With caching we typically amortize to near-zero per-token. I'll run numbers on the pilot workload you described and include KMS call counts in the spreadsheet.
[04:15] Nora Singh: DPA question: our legal asks whether Redwood will accept a data processing amendment that includes subprocessor lists and a specific audit right clause. We also want clarity on network egress responsibilities in cross-border calls.
[04:28] Maya Patel: We can provide a subprocessor list and accept an audit right with reasonable notice. On cross-border egress, we have region-routing and can pin model serving to eu-west or us-east per account; charges for cross-region egress will be billed as normal. We'll have our legal team look at any specific wording.
[04:43] Olivia Chen: Can Redwood commit to SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for admin users in the pilot? That's a gating item for procurement.
[04:50] Maya Patel: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are standard for enterprise customers; we can enable them for the pilot.
[04:55] Priya Raman: Another technical question: how are audit logs structured? We need immutable event streams with request-id, model-version, input token hash (not raw), and action traces for 7 years.
[05:08] Daniel Cho: Our logs include request-id, model id/version, timestamps, and an event trace. We avoid storing raw inputs by default, but can store hashes or encrypted blobs if you need traceability. Exports to your S3 with server-side encryption is supported.
[05:20] Liam O'Connor: Quick note on SLAs — for Dedicated we have tiered latency/availability targets. For the pilot we propose a best-effort SLO and then discuss formal SLA upon committed capacity.
[05:32] Samir Patel: That works. Finance will sign off on a pilot with capped spend, not an open committed contract, until security and KMS questions are closed.
[05:40] Nora Singh: Procurement also wants an onboarding timeline: how long to stand up a pilot with KMS integrated?
[05:46] Maya Patel: With minimal legal redlines and access, 2–3 weeks to get a pilot environment for masked data; for full KMS integration with HSM proof-of-concept add 1–2 additional weeks.
[05:58] Olivia Chen: Is there any precedent where Redwood accepted a DPA variant that prohibits vendor-side key escrow? We need that for some of our regulated products.
[06:08] Maya Patel: We've done variants where keys are customer-only with a sidecar pattern. We'll surface that to legal as a template.
[06:16] Evan Morales: If we do a sidecar pattern inside our VPC, who maintains that sidecar? Our preference is customer-managed; Redwood can provide the container image and runbook.
[06:26] Daniel Cho: Correct, customer-managed sidecar is typical. We provide images, helm charts, and a runbook. For private on-prem installs we can also recommend network policies.
[06:36] Priya Raman: Any change to latency for sidecar? We need numbers for p95.
[06:41] Daniel Cho: Expect a 20–80ms additional delta depending on KMS latency and RPC hops — we'll measure in the pilot.
[06:50] Samir Patel: For billing, can we get a commitment on a pilot spend cap and a billing cadence?
[06:56] Maya Patel: We'll propose a capped estimate for the pilot with weekly usage reports and a soft stop if spend hits 80% of cap. That'll be in the spreadsheet.
[07:06] Nora Singh: Okay let's recap next steps.
[07:10] Maya Patel: Recap: Redwood to share SOC2 and infra diagram, provide pilot pricing spreadsheet including KMS call scenarios, provide DPA variant template for customer-only keys, and propose dates for pilot kickoff. Customer to share scoped PII set, KMS requirements and initial budget cap.
[07:28] Priya Raman: Sounds good. Any competitors on the table? We did speak briefly with MajorCloudAI — but their offering didn't support sidecar BYOK as cleanly.
[07:39] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll follow up offline.
[07:43] Olivia Chen: I'll circulate internal legal redlines after the call.
[07:47] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll send the pack in a day or two.
[07:50] Meeting end.
